check.reason: the tap mask is a structural property of the wiring -- which of the 32 flops' D nets are driven by an XOR rather than by the neighbouring stage's Q -- not a value carried on any observable bus, so there is no bus_at_cycle/bus_equals_when check to write. It is checked instead by this puzzle's own bake assertion, which inspects the extracted netlist's Q-to-D adjacency directly and confirms exactly three XOR interruptions at the tap positions this mask predicts.

10**12 cycles cannot be simulated in the time this bakes in. The value is state = M^(N+1) . seed over GF(2), where M is the Galois LFSR's 32x32 linear transition map for mask 0xA3000000, seed is 0x13579BDF, N = 10**12, and the +1 matches the pack's cycle-0-origin convention (cycle N is the design's state after N+1 clock edges past reset, same convention as puzzle 1). Computed by repeated-squaring matrix exponentiation and cross-checked bit-for-bit against direct RTL and netlist simulation for every N from 0 to 4099.

reset.note: One cycle with rst_n low clears the async-set and async-reset flops to the seed 0x13579BDF. Every subsequent cycle runs with rst_n high and enable high -- the design free-runs with no stimulus.

hint: The 32 flops form a single chain once you look past each one's own clock-enable mux (every flop's D is mux(enable, hold-at-Q, real-next-value); the real-next-value is the interesting input). Three flops take their real-next-value from an XOR instead of the neighbouring stage's Q -- those are the taps, and the XOR's other input is the same flop in all three cases.
